title: Invertible augmented Cech units force completeness
statement: For a small ringed site and finite type ideal with a local extended Cech description, an isomorphism of the actual augmented Cech unit for a single object implies local derived completeness.

proof.text: Localization is sectionwise flat, hence its module sheafification is flat. Multiplication identifies the tensor square of the localization with itself; sheafification preserves this tensor comparison. Thus tensoring the localization unit by the localization is invertible. The associated localized two-term complex, supported in degrees zero and one with invertible differential, is acyclic.

The ring complex, localization two-term factors, and localization concentrated in degree zero are K-flat by bounded-above termwise flatness. Inductively the extended Cech complex is K-flat. After localizing at the first generator, its first factor is acyclic and K-flatness of the remaining tensor factors preserves this acyclicity.

Apply K-flat derived Hom currying to the localization complex and the extended Cech complex. Their total tensor is acyclic, so its derived object is zero; exactness in the contravariant input makes derived Hom from it zero. Consequently the Cech completion of any derived object is complete for its first generator.

On every finite generating slice, put any chosen generator first by a transposition of the generating list. Restrict the invertible completion unit and use the local extended Cech description and the restriction comparison for derived internal Hom. This identifies the restricted object with a Cech completion, giving vanishing from each generator localization.

Choose a finite generating covering family. Every ideal section is locally a linear combination of these generators, including the empty generating family. The complete-element ideals are stable under restriction, contain these local spans, and satisfy covering descent. Therefore every ideal section is complete. Finally use the fraction/sequential localization comparison to obtain exactly the declared local derived ideal completeness predicate.

lean.statement:
theorem ringedExtendedCech_unit_isIso_implies_complete
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O))]
    [∀ U : C, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (ringedSiteModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose (J.over U) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj (O.over U)))]
    (I : ringedSiteModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O))
    (ι : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O))
    [Mono ι] [I.IsFiniteType]
    (K : ringedSiteComplex O) (ε : K ⟶ ringedSiteRingComplex O)
    (hK : HasLocalExtendedCechDescription O I ι K ε)
    (E : ringedSiteDerived O) :
    IsIso (ringedCechCompletionUnit O K ε E) →
      IsLocallyDerivedRingedIdealComplete O I ι E
